subject: Clarifying what gets erased when: request vs. model-answer lifecycle
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@novacorp.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: security@novacorp.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: what do you keep by default (requests vs. answers)?

Hi Aditya,

We're reviewing vendors for a pilot and have a short list of items for our security review. Two related items:

1) By default, what does Redwood retain for hosted API calls? Specifically: are raw prompts (user input) stored? are generated outputs stored? does streaming change retention?
2) How can we opt out or request deletion of a subset of session artifacts (e.g., delete all model answers for an API key)? What's the standard SLA for completing erasure requests?

I've attached our questionnaire (first tab is the core ask). Can you point me at the canonical policy or provide a short, plain-language answer we can include in our vendor security assessment?

Thanks,
Sara Lin
Information Security
NovaCorp
Attachment: Nova-Security-Questionnaire.xlsx (spreadsheet, 56KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@novacorp.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: what do you keep by default (requests vs. answers)?

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear questions and the attachment. Short answer up front, then a few clarifying bullets:

Short answer (plain language):
- For hosted API customers using the default settings, Redwood retains request artifacts (user inputs/prompts) and generated outputs for 30 days.
- Streaming vs non-streaming does not change the default retention window for stored artifacts. Streams are assembled server-side; if the customer has not opted out, the assembled output is retained the same way as a non-streamed response.

Clarifying details and options:
- What counts as a "request artifact": request headers/body (including prompt text, system messages, tool calls), any uploaded attachments passed to the API, and metadata (IP, timestamp) used for diagnostics.
- What counts as a "generated output": the final model tokens returned (complete responses), model scores/metadata we surface for observability, and any reranking results.
- Ephemeral runtime caches (KV cache used for a single live session that is not configured to be persisted) are not kept past the immediate session unless the customer enables persistent session caching.
- Attachments and large artifacts: file uploads are stored in our object store and follow a longer retention by default (90 days) because they are frequently used for inspection and troubleshooting; they can be included in erasure requests.

How to opt out or request deletions:
- Self-serve: For org-level persistence control, customers can enable the "no_persist_by_default" setting in Console which prevents storing prompts/outputs for new requests (note: this reduces available observability data).
- API-level: include header x-redwood-store: false on requests to prevent storage for that call. (Works for both streaming and non-streaming.)
- Manual erasure: we accept erasure requests via Support with a ticket. Standard SLA for hosted API erasure completion is 72 hours for simple queries (single API key) and up to 7 business days for broader scopes (multi-key, archived artifacts).

Compliance notes:
- We provide an audit trail for erasure actions and can supply proof of deletion for vendor assessments (see runbook link below). For Dedicated/Private deployments customers can set custom retention via config.

I'll let Kim and Karthik add the technical edge-cases (logs vs. backups, tombstone timing). Happy to produce a one-page statement you can include in the questionnaire.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Director, Product (Redwood Inference)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@novacorp.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: what do you keep by default (requests vs. answers)? — technical addendum

Hi Sara — Kimberly from Platform here, adding the technical specifics Aditya promised. TL;DR: the 30-day window is the default retention for request/response artifacts in hosted; there are a few internal retention layers to be aware of.

Technical details:
- Primary store: request/response rows are stored in our telemetry database; these rows are soft-deleted (tombstoned) when the retention window expires. Tombstone processing runs nightly; tombstones are purged from primary DB within 72 hours after mark-for-deletion.
- Backups & snapshots: nightly backups are retained for disaster recovery; erased records are excluded from new backups but may exist in prior backups. For hosted customers, we offer a documented backup scrub process for erasure events — we remove relevant items from snapshots within our backup retention policy (up to 30 days) and record proof of scrub.
- Caches and ephemeral artifacts: live KV caches are in-memory by default; if a customer opts into persistent session caching these are stored in Redis with TTL matching the configured session retention.
- Large file attachments: stored in object storage (S3-compatible) with lifecycle rules. Default lifecycle: 90 days then transition to cold archive for another 180 days unless deleted sooner. Erasure requests include object-store deletion and a confirmation when completed.
- Logs/diagnostic traces: we keep structured logs for 90 days; they include request identifiers but not full prompt text unless debug-mode was enabled. We can provide scoped log redaction upon request but it is a distinct procedure from the core erasure flow.

Edge cases and recommended language for assessments:
- "Redwood’s hosted default retention for request and generated-output artifacts is 30 days. Attachments follow a default 90-day object-store lifecycle. Customers may opt out of persistence via org or API-level controls. Erasure requests are completed within 72 hours to 7 business days depending on scope; we provide audit evidence on completion."

If you want, I can convert that into a single-paragraph vendor-ready answer and attach a PDF.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Engineer, Platform
Attachment: Retention-Statement-Novacorp.pdf (draft vendor statement, 8KB)

- We'll likely want to test the x-redwood-store: false header on a small test API key in our pilot — can you confirm that header also suppresses storage of attachments passed as multipart form data?

If you can drop the PDF into a shared location or attach here we'll include it with our security packet. Thanks again.

Best,
